newsitem.title: UK: BAA to dismiss errant cargo service firms.
newsitem.headline: BAA to dismiss errant cargo service firms.

text.p: BAA Plc is threatening to expel any members of its "London Cargo Promise" scheme which do not meet agreed minimum performance standards, said its head of cargo development Ian Robinson.
"Companies which fail to deal adequately with performance shortfalls will be required to withdraw from the scheme...they will be struck off," he told Reuters.
All cargo ground service providers at the three BAA London airports -- Heathrow, Gatwick and Stansted -- are signatories to the scheme, which was launched in 1995.
"We think achievievement of 100 percent participation by these companies is phenomenal, unique in the international air cargo industry," he said.

Robinson added that so far there had been complaints from shippers about three members of the scheme, all of which are involved in truck handling. These companies had been informed of the complaints and were now rectifying the problems.
"We understand that the areas of off-loading and loading at airports are the ones most vulnerable to criticism and which are the most open to improvement," he noted.

"This has especially been the case at Heathrow. But on March 21, a new BAA-built multi-storey carpark will open at the airport's cargo centre, which will remove cars which currently park in the 'horseshoe'-shaped area between cargo terminals," he said.
This would give drivers more room to manoeuvre their vehicles hopefully ending the loading and off-loading problems caused by traffic congestion.

Under the "London Cargo Promise", companies agree to meet specific targets covering flown/shipped-as-booked times, close-out acceptance times, truck handling, cargo availability, documentation, customs clearance and connected-as-booked and transhipment times. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax 5017
